    18	
    19	μMongo is a Python MongoDB ODM. It inception comes from two needs:
    20	the lack of async ODM and the difficulty to do document (un)serialization
    21	with existing ODMs.
    22	
    23	From this point, μMongo made a few design choices:
    24	
    25	- Stay close to the standards MongoDB driver to keep the same API when possible:
    26	  use ``find({"field": "value"})`` like usual but retrieve your data nicely OO wrapped !
    27	- Work with multiple drivers (PyMongo_, TxMongo_, motor_asyncio_ and mongomock_ for the moment)
    28	- Tight integration with Marshmallow_ serialization library to easily
    29	  dump and load your data with the outside world
    30	- i18n integration to localize validation error messages
    31	- Free software: MIT license
    32	- Test with 90%+ coverage ;-)
    33	
    34	.. _PyMongo: https://api.mongodb.org/python/current/
    35	.. _TxMongo: https://txmongo.readthedocs.org/en/latest/
    36	.. _motor_asyncio: https://motor.readthedocs.org/en/stable/
    37	.. _mongomock: https://github.com/vmalloc/mongomock
    38	.. _Marshmallow: http://marshmallow.readthedocs.org
    39	
    40	Quick example
    41	
    42	.. code-block:: python
    43	
    44	    from datetime import datetime
    45	    from pymongo import MongoClient
    46	    from umongo import Instance, Document, fields, validate
    47	
    48	    db = MongoClient().test
    49	    instance = Instance(db)
    50	
    51	    @instance.register
    52	    class User(Document):
    53	        email = fields.EmailField(required=True, unique=True)
    54	        birthday = fields.DateTimeField(validate=validate.Range(min=datetime(1900, 1, 1)))
    55	        friends = fields.ListField(fields.ReferenceField("User"))
    56	
    57	        class Meta:
    58	            collection = db.user
    59	
    60	    # Make sure that unique indexes are created
    61	    User.ensure_indexes()
    62	
    63	    goku = User(email='goku@sayen.com', birthday=datetime(1984, 11, 20))
    64	    goku.commit()

    66	    vegeta.commit()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Additional edge case tests for the _extract_marshmallow_field_params fix.
"""

from umongo import fields


def test_various_field_types():
    """Test that the fix works with various field types."""
    
    field_types = [
        fields.StrField,
        fields.IntField,
        fields.FloatField,
        fields.BoolField,
        fields.DateTimeField,
    ]
    
    for field_cls in field_types:
        print(f"Testing {field_cls.__name__}...")
        
        # Test basic field
        field = field_cls()
        params = field._extract_marshmallow_field_params(mongo_world=False)
        
        # Should not contain load_from or dump_to
        assert 'load_from' not in params, f"{field_cls.__name__} still copies load_from"
        assert 'dump_to' not in params, f"{field_cls.__name__} still copies dump_to"
        
        # Should contain expected attributes
        expected = {'validate', 'required', 'allow_none', 'load_only', 'dump_only', 'error_messages', 'default', 'missing'}
        assert expected.issubset(set(params.keys())), f"{field_cls.__name__} missing expected keys: {expected - set(params.keys())}"
        
        print(f"  ✅ {field_cls.__name__} passed")


def test_with_metadata():
    """Test that metadata is still properly copied."""
    
    field = fields.StrField(metadata={'description': 'A test field', 'example': 'test'})
    params = field._extract_marshmallow_field_params(mongo_world=False)
    
    # Metadata should be included
    assert 'description' in params, "Metadata not copied"
    assert params['description'] == 'A test field', "Metadata value incorrect"
    assert 'example' in params, "Metadata not copied"
    assert params['example'] == 'test', "Metadata value incorrect"
    
    print("✅ Metadata copying works correctly")


def test_mongo_world_attribute():
    """Test that mongo_world parameter works correctly."""
    
    # Test without attribute
    field1 = fields.StrField()
    params_no_attr = field1._extract_marshmallow_field_params(mongo_world=True)
    assert 'attribute' not in params_no_attr, "Attribute added when it shouldn't be"
    
    # Test with attribute
    field2 = fields.StrField(attribute='mongo_name')
    params_with_attr = field2._extract_marshmallow_field_params(mongo_world=True)
    assert 'attribute' in params_with_attr, "Attribute not added when it should be"
    assert params_with_attr['attribute'] == 'mongo_name', "Attribute value incorrect"
    
    # Test mongo_world=False should never have attribute
    params_no_mongo = field2._extract_marshmallow_field_params(mongo_world=False)
    assert 'attribute' not in params_no_mongo, "Attribute added in non-mongo world"
    
    print("✅ Mongo world attribute handling works correctly")


def test_marshmallow_attributes():
    """Test that marshmallow_default and marshmallow_missing work correctly."""
    
    field = fields.StrField(default='test_default', marshmallow_default='marshmallow_default')
    
    params = field._extract_marshmallow_field_params(mongo_world=False)
    
    # Should use marshmallow_default, not the raw default
    assert params['default'] == 'marshmallow_default' or callable(params['default']), "marshmallow_default not used"
    assert params['missing'] == 'marshmallow_default' or callable(params['missing']), "marshmallow_default not used for missing"
    
    print("✅ Marshmallow default/missing handling works correctly")


if __name__ == "__main__":

    test_mongo_world_attribute()
    test_marshmallow_attributes()

    12	# tsfresh
    13	
    14	This repository contains the *TSFRESH* python package. The abbreviation stands for
    15	
    16	*"Time Series Feature extraction based on scalable hypothesis tests"*.
    17	
    18	The package contains many feature extraction methods and a robust feature selection algorithm.
    19	
    20	## Spend less time on feature engineering
    21	
    22	Data Scientists often spend most of their time either cleaning data or building features.
    23	While we cannot change the first thing, the second can be automated.
    24	*TSFRESH* frees your time spent on building features by extracting them automatically.
    25	Hence, you have more time to study the newest deep learning paper, read hacker news or build better models.
    26	
    27	
    28	## Automatic extraction of 100s of features
    29	
    30	*TSFRESH* automatically extracts 100s of features from time series.
    31	Those features describe basic characteristics of the time series such as the number of peaks, the average or maximal value or more complex features such as the time reversal symmetry statistic.
    32	
    33	![The features extracted from a exemplary time series](docs/images/introduction_ts_exa_features.png)
    34	
    35	The set of features can then be used to construct statistical or machine learning models on the time series to be used for example in regression or
    36	classification tasks.
    37	
    38	## Forget irrelevant features
    39	
    40	Time series often contain noise, redundancies or irrelevant information.
    41	As a result most of the extracted features will not be useful for the machine learning task at hand.
    42	
    43	To avoid extracting irrelevant features, the *TSFRESH* package has a built-in filtering procedure.
    44	This filtering procedure evaluates the explaining power and importance of each characteristic for the regression or classification tasks at hand.
    45	
    46	It is based on the well developed theory of hypothesis testing and uses a multiple test procedure.
    47	As a result the filtering process mathematically controls the percentage of irrelevant extracted features.
    48	
    49	The  *TSFRESH* package is described in the following open access paper
    50	
    51	* Christ, M., Braun, N., Neuffer, J. and Kempa-Liehr A.W. (2018).
    52	   _Time Series FeatuRe Extraction on basis of Scalable Hypothesis tests (tsfresh -- A Python package)._
    53	   Neurocomputing 307 (2018) 72-77, [doi:10.1016/j.neucom.2018.03.067](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2018.03.067).
    54	
    55	The FRESH algorithm is described in the following whitepaper
    56	
    57	* Christ, M., Kempa-Liehr, A.W. and Feindt, M. (2017).  
    58	    _Distributed and parallel time series feature extraction for industrial big data applications._  
    59	    ArXiv e-print 1610.07717,  [https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.07717](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.07717).
    60	
    61	
    62	## Advantages of tsfresh
    63	
    64	*TSFRESH* has several selling points, for example
    65	
    66	1. it is field tested
    67	2. it is unit tested
    68	3. the filtering process is statistically/mathematically correct
    69	4. it has a comprehensive documentation
    70	5. it is compatible with sklearn, pandas and numpy
    71	6. it allows anyone to easily add their favorite features
    72	7. it both runs on your local machine or even on a cluster
    73	
    74	## Next steps
    75	
    76	If you are interested in the technical workings, go to see our comprehensive Read-The-Docs documentation at [http://tsfresh.readthedocs.io](http://tsfresh.readthedocs.io).
    77	
    78	The algorithm, especially the filtering part are also described in the paper mentioned above.
    79	
    80	If you have some questions or feedback you can find the developers in the [gitter chatroom.](https://gitter.im/tsfresh/Lobby?utm_source=share-link&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=share-link)
    81	
    82	We appreciate any contributions, if you are interested in helping us to make *TSFRESH* the biggest archive of feature extraction methods in python, just head over to our [How-To-Contribute](http://tsfresh.readthedocs.io/en/latest/text/how_to_contribute.html) instructions.
